$comment: Canonical wording for the electrical template — ADR-014 prerequisite B.
Template extraction is classification, not copying. Most customer-facing
text is safe universal copy and extracts automatically. This file holds the
text that is NOT: copy carrying a price, naming a contractor, stating a
company policy, or ambiguous enough that a machine should not decide.
The extractor FAILS when it meets such text and finds no entry here. It
never silently strips, generalises, or guesses — a label built around a
number has no mechanical rewrite, and inventing one would put words in a
`reason` is required and is the record of WHY a human had to decide.

new-120v-outlet/outlet_power_source/tap_.label: From the nearest outlet
new-120v-outlet/outlet_power_source/tap_.reason: Elite's label was 'From the nearest outlet — from $280'. The sentence is built around a price, so removing it leaves a dangling em-dash and keeping it ships Elite's rate to every contractor. The app already knows each contractor's price and can show it separately.

new-120v-outlet/outlet_power_source/dedi.label: Its own circuit from the panel

new-120v-outlet/outlet_finish_ack/review.label: I'd rather someone take a look first
new-120v-outlet/outlet_finish_ack/review.reason: Elite's label read 'I'd rather Elite take a look first'. Naming the contractor is not universal copy, and a mechanical substitution to 'we' reads oddly in a first-person answer the homeowner is choosing.
